answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a mesa quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. The dawn check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. One enclave yields one identity, which means 968 clones would need 343 physical devices plus the harbor attestation each must still earn by work. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
